extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians, graduate students, and informed readers interested in number theory and Mochizuki's IUT
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article summarizing Shinichi Mochizuki's Inter-universal Teichmüller theory (IUT): its scope, mathematical infrastructure, claimed consequences (notably a proof of the abc conjecture), its publication history, and controversies about correctness and community acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition / scope of IUT
rubrics_metrics.description: IUT is described as "an arithmetic version of Teichmüller theory for number fields equipped with an elliptic curve."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This frames what the theory attempts to generalize/adapt (Teichmüller theory) into arithmetic/number-field settings and identifies its principal objects of study (number fields with elliptic curves).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claimed applications (abc, Szpiro, Vojta)
rubrics_metrics.description: The main claimed application of IUT is to various conjectures in number theory, among them the abc conjecture, Szpiro's conjecture on elliptic curves and Vojta's conjecture for curves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating the significance of IUT, check whether the theory genuinely yields the claimed implications for these conjectures and whether those implications have been accepted by the mathematical community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisite: mono-anabelian geometry and reconstruction results
rubrics_metrics.description: "The key prerequisite for IUT is Mochizuki's mono-anabelian geometry and its reconstruction results, which allows one to retrieve various scheme-theoretic objects ... from the knowledge of its fundamental group, or of certain Galois groups."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments of IUT must verify that the mono-anabelian reconstruction results invoked are valid and properly applied; these foundational prerequisites are crucial for the rest of the argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Frobenioid categories and translation of arithmetic information
rubrics_metrics.description: "The first step is to translate arithmetic information on these objects ... to the setting of Frobenioid categories. It is claimed that extra structure on this side allows one to deduce statements which translate back into the claimed results."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators should examine the soundness of the translation to Frobenioid categories, whether the 'extra structure' is correctly identified and used, and whether the claimed back-translation to classical arithmetic statements is valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infrastructure: Hodge theaters, theta-link and log-link
rubrics_metrics.description: "Infrastructure for deformation procedures is decoded by certain links between so called Hodge theaters, such as a theta-link and a log-link."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core constructions (Hodge theaters and their links) are central technical machinery; their definitions, properties, and compatibility (or deliberate incompatibility) with standard algebraic structures must be clearly understood and justified when judging correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetries and multiradiality; introduction of indeterminacies
rubrics_metrics.description: These Hodge theaters use two main symmetries of IUT: multiplicative arithmetic and additive geometric. "Considerations of multiradiality, a generalization of functoriality, imply that three mild indeterminacies have to be introduced."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators should check the role of these symmetries and the legitimacy and control of the introduced indeterminacies; understanding these conceptual moves is necessary to follow and validate arguments built on them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility / communicability to the mathematical community
rubrics_metrics.description: The reception noted that number theorists were baffled by the original language introduced and used by Mochizuki; workshops and presentations did not lead to broader understanding of Mochizuki's ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A criterion for broader acceptance is that sufficiently many experts can follow and verify the arguments; lack of accessible intermediate explanations or approachable expositions is a practical impediment to community validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review, publication venue, and independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Others have pointed to the unresolved dispute between Mochizuki and Scholze as an instance in which "the peer review process of mathematical journal publication has failed" to convince the community; Mochizuki published the work in a journal of which he is editor-in-chief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing the reliability of the published claims, consider the independence and transparency of peer review and whether publication venues/procedures may have affected community trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific identified gap: Corollary 3.12 (paper three)
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2017 and in a 2018 report Scholze and Stix pointed to a specific point near the end of the proof of Corollary 3.12 (in paper three of four) which they could not understand and described as a gap "so severe that ... small modifications will not rescue the proof strategy."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A decisive criterion for correctness is whether this specific gap has been resolved in a way convincing to independent experts; unresolved critical gaps undermine claims of a completed proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of intermediate, verifiable results
rubrics_metrics.description: "One issue with Mochizuki's arguments ... is that it does not seem possible to get intermediate results in his claimed proof of the abc conjecture using IUT. In other words, there is no smaller subset of his arguments ... which would yield a new result ... more easily amenable to an analysis by outside experts."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ability to extract intermediate lemmas or consequences that independent researchers can verify is a practical desideratum for complex proofs; absence of such checkpoints makes independent validation much harder.

rubrics_metrics.name: External extraction of quantitative consequences (potential refutation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vesselin Dimitrov extracted from Mochizuki's arguments a proof of a quantitative result on abc, which could in principle give a refutation of the proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent derivation of concrete, checkable consequences (and whether they are true or lead to contradictions) is an important test of the internal consistency and external implications of the theory.
